parts:
Hi Mona.

First, a couple things.  Please reply to the group email list, not me directly so that others can learn from these exchanges.  Secondly, please give the commands you used in R.  When you say 'Then i used this new fuction and did fitPLM', I don't know exactly what you actually did.  I can make some guesses, but it would be helpful to have your commands.

A couple things to look at:
http://groups.google.com/group/aroma-affymetrix/web/human-exon-array-analysis
(this gives instructions on how to do a standard exon array analysis ... note: there is no 'bgAdjustRma' there, so your instructions may not be up to date)

Below is a 'standard' exon array analysis that I have done:

verbose <- Arguments$getVerbose(-8); timestampOn(verbose)
name <- "affy_3_mix"
chip2<- "HuEx-1_0-st-v2"
cs2 <- AffymetrixCelSet$fromName(name, chipType=chip2)
bc2 <- RmaBackgroundCorrection(cs2)
csBC2 <- process(bc2)
coreChipType <- paste(chip2, "core", sep=",")
chip2o<- AffymetrixCdfFile$fromChipType(chip2)
cdf <- AffymetrixCdfFile$fromChipType(coreChipType)
setCdf(csBC2, cdf)
qn2 <- QuantileNormalization(csBC2, typesToUpdate="pm")
csN2 <- process(qn2, verbose=verbose) #time required
plm2.merge <- ExonRmaPlm(csN2, mergeGroups=TRUE)
fit(plm2.merge, verbose=verbose) #time required

Hope that helps.

Mark

parts:
Hi Mona.

I can't spot anything obvious ... however ...

> plm2.merge <- ExonRmaPlm(csN2, mergeGroups=TRUE)
> fit(plm2.merge, verbose=verbose) #time required, ###### it didn't take
> even few seconds for my 7 samples

... this worries me. This should take some time. Let's track this
down. Try a couple of things for me:

1. When you fit the model, add the verbose=verbose to the command:
plm2.merge <- ExonRmaPlm(csN2, mergeGroups=TRUE,verbose=verbose)
This will spit out a bunch more output to the screen and might
identify what is happening.

2. Try and pull out the normalized data (i.e. from the 'csN2' object,
do a 'readUnits' or 'readData', whichever you prefer) and look at the
data for a couple units. For example, it looks like the fitting
might've worked for 2315588, but not for the rest. I'm interested to
know what data went into those fits and that could lead us to the
problem.

3. Sometimes when starting up, there are files are directories that
get left behind from previous analyses, so another possibility is to
re-run everything, including the background adjustment and
normalization. By default, aroma.affymetrix looks in the relevant
directories and checks whether have been run, but you can force it to
rerun by using force=T in the 'process' and 'fit' commands.

Cheers,
Mark
